claim: Neural links augment or bypass specialized brain functions
originalWording: Neural links augment or bypass specialized brain functions

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)
sources.locator: Computers and communications in 2029: neural pathways

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: High-bandwidth neural links materially replace or augment specialized brain-region functions.
strict.rationale: The 2029 deadline is future. Clinical sensory implants and neural-interface research support partial progress, not the broadly perfected high-bandwidth cognitive bypass described.

evidence.title: What educators need to know about cochlear implants — FDA
evidence.note: Cochlear implants do not restore normal hearing. Used to correct a medical error in our intake, not to manufacture a Kurzweil forecast.

evidence.title: NIH: Complete cell map of a whole mammalian brain
evidence.note: Mouse cell atlas, not a functional emulation of the entire human brain.

evidence.title: Dorkenwald et al.: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain
evidence.note: Adult fruit-fly connectome. Species, wiring map and functional cognitive model must not be conflated.
